reviewed.review: Dammit, this is still great. It still actually looks really good, which is especially hard considering the era it was made in, which was the early digital transition — there are a lot of things from that era that end up looking pretty trashy. Fabulous opening, too. It's a great episode, a great piece of Kon's work. And it's always interesting to see someone who primarily works in one medium translate to another — in this case, a film director going and doing a 13-episode TV series. So I'm very happy that we're watching/reviewing this again, and I'm definitely looking forward to seeing where this crazy show goes, one I haven't watched in over 20 years.

I finally watched an episode of this, so this is an out-of-order review. S-tier. It's fabulous. At least episode one was incredible—so well done, one of those things where you watch it and you're like, "yeah, just make good anime and everything in the world will be better."
This is a show I still fondly remember watching quite a few times and would be happy to go back to.

reviewed.titleJP: ソードアート・オンライン
reviewed.review: Okay, so this is a real show here. It has some highs, some lows, and it really was a huge spawning point for this whole genre. What I would say is good here is the OST, the OP, and the overall animation quality. The first half of the first season is pretty fun, but that's like ~6 eps. The second half of the first season gets less good. Then there's eps 13-24 of season 1; boy, just terrible. The animation was still good, but it went into such weird story stuff and totally lost me. Then there's every season after that, which was just worse. So I'll give it a 3, splitting a 5 for the first few eps and a 1 for everything after that. I'm sure I'm being too kind to this show, but I'm a bit of a softie.
